captive-mother.name: Captive mother
captive-mother.role: young captive mother defending her infant, digs the grave
captive-mother.look: a young woman in her twenties, thin, hair tied back, ragged colonial dress and shawl, mud on her hands, a baby strapped to her back

older-captive.name: Older former captive
older-captive.role: older woman who chose to live in the woods, serves the poisoned broth
older-captive.look: an older woman in her sixties, weathered face, grey hair under a plain cap, a worn wool cloak and apron

english-scout.name: English scout
english-scout.role: colonial scout who carries a severed hand as a trophy and dies poisoned
english-scout.look: a rugged English militiaman in his thirties, beard, leather jerkin and wide-brimmed hat, musket at his side

wet-meadow.look: a wet freezing meadow at the edge of a dark forest, mud, bedrock showing through the soil, night

forest-clearing.look: a forest clearing in colonial Massachusetts, tall pines and oaks, dappled light, later the apple tree

spine.claim: The woods remember more than the people who pass through them: a captive mother buries a poisoned scout in a wet colonial meadow.
A single apple seed inside the scout becomes a tree that outlives every family that tries to own the land.
Each generation builds on the same ground and repeats the same violence in new clothes.
The trees, not the people, are the ones who keep the record of the land.
